key_insight: Seemingly different short mode-evolution coupler designs share one two-mode design space, with equivalent counter-diabatic realizations offering the same bandwidth.
engineering_relevance: A lithography-aware rule enables broadband, compact optical couplers without numerical optimization by narrowing waveguide spacing at the anticrossing and applying exact counter-diabatic correction.
method: Unify width, spacing, and axis-bending controls using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory.
Relate bandwidth to the integrated light–steering-field misalignment on the Bloch sphere.
Validate the design rule with polymer-platform BPM simulations and compare against particle swarm optimization.
evidence_signal: BPM simulations predict >99% transfer across 274 nm for a 500 µm coupler with a 1.05 µm minimum edge gap, versus 150 nm for a fixed-spacing-reference CD design at nearly the same gap; 3D BPM supports the conclusions.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation validation rather than fabricated-device measurements, leaving fabrication tolerance and experimental performance to be established.
paper_title: Unified design of short mode-evolution couplers
